title: Autosuggest Applier: safety choreography for gated canary and rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a safe orchestration layer for the Optimize service's automated batching/caching suggestions so recommendations can be auto-applied under strict governance. This ticket covers the choreography for gated rollouts, simulated canaries, runtime telemetry gates, operator approval hooks, and an automated revert path when regressions are detected.

Scope:
- Design the rollout state machine (stages: dry-run -> simulated canary -> limited apply -> expanded apply -> full apply), with operator-latch points.
- Build an event-driven enactor that can apply Optimize suggestions to runtime config with tenant-scoped constraints and API auth.
- Integrate a canary runner that synthesizes traffic and compares key metrics (p99 latency, token cost per request, quality regressions based on eval prompts) against baseline.
- Implement telemetry gates that require metrics to stay within thresholds over a sliding window before progressing.
- Add an explicit human-approval step (Console + webhook) for high-risk changes and a fast rollback trigger.
- Document a rollback playbook that includes automated rollback, extra tracing, and postmortem triggers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Enactor can move a single tenant through the staged rollout with no manual config changes.
- Canary runner produces per-stage diff reports and a pass/fail signal for gating.
- If any gate fails, enactor halts and, depending on severity, auto-rolls back to previous config.
- Operator can override an automated halt with a documented justification recorded in the audit log.
- All applied changes are recorded in tenant-level audit logs and surfaced in Console with links to the canary report and PRs.
- E2E tests simulating regressions cause rollback within defined SLOs.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not include global multitenant orchestration (we'll pilot on dedicated + hosted with canary tenant groups).
- It does not implement model-quality retraining or automatic prompt rewrites.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Stronger safety (longer canary windows, more simulation traffic) increases time-to-benefit for cost reductions. We default to conservative windows for the first two quarters.
- Tight coupling with Console simplifies operator flows but increases release coordination; we'll expose enactor APIs so Console and SRE can evolve independently.

Key metrics for telemetry gates:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 delta <= configured threshold (default p99 delta <= +10ms over baseline).
- Cost: tokens-per-request delta <= -1% (we expect cost down) but reject if cost increases by >2%.
- Quality: eval prompt BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity drop not exceeding 0.6% absolute or similarity delta >0.02 triggers fail.
- Errors: 5xx rate increase <= 0.05% absolute.

Rollout plan (pilot):
1) Dry-run: generate a simulated apply and store planned config in staging.
2) Simulated canary: run deterministic synthetic traffic and compare telemetry in sandbox.
3) Tenant canary: apply to 1-3 low-risk tenants for 1 hour; monitor gates.
4) Targeted cohort: expand to 10% of tenants tied to predictable workloads for 6 hours.
5) Full: roll out remainder with rolling waves.

Rollback playbook:
- Immediate auto-rollback if gate fails at any stage (revert config + invalidate KV cache entries introduced by change).
- If operator overrides, require a 2nd-seat approver and post-rollout monitoring escalation.
- Post-failure: run forensics job to snapshot traces, token-level cost deltas, and quality-eval artifacts and attach to incident.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Enforcer service: new small service to sequence state machine and call runtime config APIs. (ENG workstream)
- Canary harness: extend existing test harness to run synthetic prompts, capture metrics and compute diffs. (TEST + ENG)
- Telemetry gate engine: declarative gate specs + metric adapters to Console metrics backends. (OBS + ENG)
- Console UX: approval modal, canary report viewer, override workflow. (PM + DX)
- Audit & security: ensure KMS usage for config artifacts, RBAC checks, and immutable audit entries. (SEC)

Dependencies: ENG-41876, ENG-24652, PM-330 (design alignment), DES-98 (console UX sketches)
